summary: In 2021, a campaign exploiting on-premises Microsoft Exchange servers was attributed to China-linked state-sponsored group HAFNIUM, also known as Silk Typhoon, which left over 88,000 backdoors.
Huntress and the FBI removed web shells at scale using a Rule 41 warrant with cloud provider cooperation, and suspected co-conspirator Xu Zewei was arrested in Milan in July 2025.
The FBI reported at least a dozen cyber actor extraditions in the first half of 2026 and is dismantling criminal infrastructure, including phishing platforms and residential proxy networks.

6e973c6d2d674415.title: From Screen Share to Root Access: Breaking Down CVE-2026-43760 and CVE-2026-65400 on macOS
summary: A pre-authentication vulnerability, CVE-2026-65400, was found in macOS Screen Sharing (screensharingd). A public PoC has been released, and it is reported to allow arbitrary file reads and writes and remote code execution without authentication.
A frame length validation error in the SRP implementation causes failed authentication to be treated as successful, so the connection remains an unencrypted plaintext session.

Apple patched the issue on August 6, 2026 in macOS 26.6.1, 15.7.9, and 14.8.9. Until systems are patched, disabling Screen Sharing is recommended, and exposure is reported to be common in hosted Mac services.

033fa0936f09ffe3.title: Living off the coding agent: Two tales of tunnels and LaunchAgents
summary: Elastic Security Labs analyzed signs that a Claude Code child process on a macOS developer machine used free tunneling services to expose a local management app to the outside.
A shell under the agent sent authenticated HTTP requests through localhost.run and Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, and a LaunchAgent was configured to keep the tunnel running.
Because legitimate tools are mixed with abuse, the activity cannot be conclusively called malicious. However, credential exposure and persistence installation should be investigated as high severity.

6b1e41630c4eb94c.title: The security signal log tailing can't see: tracking npm cooldown removals with Elastic Agent
summary: Elastic Security Labs described a method for detecting changes that remove the cooldown setting from npm's .npmrc configuration.
A CEL integration of about 40 lines saves .npmrc files as snapshots every six hours to catch changes. The approach was adopted after the limits of the earlier filestream method became clear.
Only an overview is available, so attack cases and the scale of damage are unclear. Refer to the original article for the detailed detection procedure.

4160238c32ddf686.title: Invisible Attack Surface: Thousands of Industrial Control Systems Exposed Around Data Centers
summary: Trend Micro scanned areas within 1 km of more than 1,000 US data centers using Shodan to measure exposed industrial control systems (ICS).
The research identified 6,300 high-confidence building automation devices reachable from the internet, mostly using BACnet and Fox/Niagara protocols. No active exploitation was performed.
Newer data centers showed higher exposure rates, and multi-protocol gateways could give attackers access to several building systems if compromised.

5f3a71b5da3c0f43.title: Hijacking Agentic AI Part 3: How to Protect AI Agents
summary: Trend Micro researchers outlined the final defense strategy in their series on return-to-tool (RTT) attacks, a major threat to agentic AI.
RTT stems from agents operating with broader privileges than users and interpreting external data as executable instructions. The article says WAFs and container isolation alone cannot stop it.

The authors recommend layering deterministic controls (row-level security, separation of read and write agents, permission proxies, and human approval gates) with probabilistic controls (prompt hardening and classifiers), plus detection through audit logs and canary records.

5fd5037497ebdf79.title: Mac Malware Drains Crypto Wallets Via Fake CAPTCHA Scam
summary: Huntress analyzed an incident in which the ClickFix technique tricked users into pasting commands into the macOS Terminal.
A Go-based Mach-O infostealer took keychain and browser credentials, and its DRAIN function moved cryptocurrency wallet balances to attacker-controlled wallets.
The infrastructure is linked to Russia's Aeza Group, which has been sanctioned by the United States and others. The article does not specify the scale of the damage or the current response status.

49ff83397dc8a730.title: UNC6671 Rebrands: Multi-Brand Vishing Extortion Targets Financial Services and Enterprise Cloud Environments
summary: After retiring the BlackFile brand, UNC6671 continues data theft and extortion under several brands, including Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon.

The group impersonates IT help desks in vishing calls to employees' personal phones, uses fake passkey registration pages to capture credentials and MFA tokens, and then exfiltrates Microsoft 365 and Okta data.
Shared domains and identical phishing templates suggest the brands are linked. In June and July 2026, targets shifted to financial and legal sectors, and domain registration accelerated.

c30d495a07c10974.title: Shai-Hulud strikes again: CHAINDROP worm hits 400+ npm packages
summary: Elastic Security Labs identified a new Shai-Hulud campaign targeting the maintainer of the keyv package. The self-propagating worm CHAINDROP was used.
Using stolen npm credentials, the worm plants backdoors in other packages the maintainer can publish, and it executes through the preinstall hook in package.json.

More than 400 npm packages have been infected so far. There are concerns that AI tool and cloud credentials may be stolen, and revoking GitHub and npm tokens and applying a waiting period before installation are recommended.

e914be2f658836cf.title: Inside an Oracle Database SQL Injection Attack | Huntress
summary: Huntress detected credential theft activity on an endpoint hosting an Oracle database server on July 27, 2026.

The attacker gained entry through SQL injection exploiting insufficient input validation in a public web application, then stored the khunt post-exploitation toolkit inside the database as Java source.
The attacker executed OS commands from the database to obtain SYSTEM privileges and copied the SAM, SECURITY, and SYSTEM registry hives; the attacking IP was identified as 178.162.151[.]229.

472e17874338756d.title: Benchmarking the Agentic SOC: How we evaluate LLMs for security workflows
summary: Elastic Security Labs released a framework for evaluating LLMs used in agentic SOCs that perform security workflows.
General leaderboards fail to catch plausible answers given without tool calls, so the framework scores the actual order of tool calls, parameters, and results together.
The Chrysalis backdoor scenario is reproduced as a synthetic intrusion, VirusTotal verdicts are fixed using EICAR hashes, and models are compared using 21 prompts.

9126ea498559cbac.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability in Dify's Post-Login Flow: From Discovery by TrendAI Research to Fix
summary: TrendAI Research discovered an open redirect vulnerability (CVE-2026-18266, CVSS 5.4) in the post-login authentication flow of Dify, an AI app platform, and reported it through ZDI.
By abusing an unvalidated URL parameter, attackers could redirect users to an attacker-controlled site immediately after sign-in, steal authentication tokens, and impersonate users.
Dify merged the fix on July 13, 2026, and ZDI published its advisory on July 29. Operators must upgrade to v1.16.0 or later.

10c704054d18249c.title: TrendAI Intelligence Contributes to Law Enforcement Arrest of Tycoon 2FA Operators
summary: In August 2026, Singapore Police announced the arrest of two people linked to Tycoon 2FA in Punjab, Pakistan.
Tycoon 2FA is a phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform that bypasses MFA through an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) proxy to steal credentials and session cookies.
Its infrastructure was dismantled in March in an operation led by Microsoft and Europol, and this arrest is a follow-up result; four suspects remain at large abroad.

53e53e916bbd5353.title: What Cybercriminals Want from Corporate Insiders
summary: Trend Micro's two-year observation shows the insider access market is shifting from one-off opportunistic crimes to an organized economy.
Brokers offer fixed fees, profit sharing, and referral rewards, selling access, information, and services by industry.
Cases in which telecom employees enabled SIM swapping, retail refund fraud, and review manipulation on reputation platforms have been confirmed as leading to actual crimes.

00ce77945c391217.title: Bank of America Phishing Email Delivers ScreenConnect Malware
summary: A phishing email impersonating Bank of America was sent from a honeytrap account and led victims through a fake security center page to download a VBS file.
The VBS file decodes PowerShell through multi-stage base64 decoding and AES decryption, then installs ScreenConnect with administrator privileges using a UAC bypass via the ICMLuaUtil COM interface.
The installed ScreenConnect is hidden under the service name 'Windows Security' and attempts C2 connections to 217.60.195[.]167 on port 8041/tcp. The scale of damage has not been confirmed.

8b96f1a369249701.title: Malicious Cyber Activity Targeting US Water Utilities: What Operators Need to Know
summary: Water facility disruptions originating from internet-exposed devices have been reported in at least seven US states.
Most of the disruptions are attributed to misconfigurations and inadequate access controls.
The article outlines the first response measures operators should take, and detailed damage information requires review of the original source.
